newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Top Colombian lawman ousted by Supreme Court.
newsitem.headline: Top Colombian lawman ousted by Supreme Court.

text.p: Colombia's Supreme Court said on Friday it had ordered the dismissal of disgraced Attorney General Orlando Vasquez Velasquez five months after his arrest on drug corruption charges.

Supreme Court President Roberto Herrera announced the unprecedented decision at a news conference after the court voted by an overwhelming 22-1 late on Thursday to call for the immediate replacement of the country's top law officer.
In addition, Herrera said the court had banned Vasquez from holding any public office for the next five years.

Judicial sources said the court was to notify the Senate of its ruling by early next week. Approval of the order is a mere formality, however, since it is not subject to appeal and must be strictly complied with by the legislative branch.

In brief remarks to reporters on Friday, before departing on an official visit to Asia, President Ernesto Samper said he trusted Vasquez would have an opportunity to defend himself. But he conceded the ruling was binding and said he would name a possible replacement when the Senate asked him to do so.
Vasquez's defeat was a victory for Prosecutor-General Alfonso Valdivieso, an anti-drug crusader and sworn enemy of corrupt politicians with whom Vasquez has clashed repeatedly.

The dismissal stemmed, at least in part, from what authorities described as Vasquez's use of "false witnesses" to open an investigation this year into what he claimed was an illegal land deal involving Valdivieso.
More recently Vasquez, who has made no secret of his intense dislike for Valdivieso, had also accused him of using drug money to back a failed bid for the Senate in 1994.

Vasquez, a former interior minister and ruling Liberal Party senator, was released in August from a police detention facility in the capital, where he had been held since early May on charges he accepted thousands of dollars in payments from leading drug traffickers, both before and after he was sworn in as attorney general in 1994.
He has denied any wrongdoing but his U.S. travel visa was revoked in April because of his alleged links to drug lords.

Guillermo Pallomari, the self-confessed Cali drug cartel treasurer who surrendered to U.S. drug agents in the United States last year, has testified that Vasquez had closer ties with the cartel's jailed leaders than perhaps any other politician in Colombia.
Vasquez was suspended from office by the Supreme Court shortly before his arrest in May but continued to hold the title of attorney general.
